page0.text:
"Oh, right. Sakura, this is Illya.
Her Berserker got taken out, but we managed to save her. She's going to be staying with us like Tohsaka, so try to get along."
I introduce Sakura and Illya to each other.

page1.text:
"Hi, Sakura. I heard you're a daughter of the Makiris, but I won't hold that against you. You seem like you know Shirou, so I'll give you special treatment."
"...Okay. Then I'll treat you the same way."

page2.text:
"Hm?"
That's the extent of their greetings.
Illya leaves Tohsaka and walks to the living room.
As she does...
...
I see Sakura watching her with somewhat cold eyes.

page3.text:
Dinner comes and goes like a sudden storm.
...Okay, to call it a storm would be misleading.
It was more like a doldrum where you lose track of time because there's no wind, and then it ends before you know it.
Anyway, it was a dinner fraught with tension.

page4.text:
"Should I make dinner, then? It'll be like having soba noodles for housewarming."
With that, Tohsaka starts cooking on her own, and I'm forced to admit that she's better at it than me. Sakura's Western-style cooking might barely measure up.

page5.text:
"T-Tohsaka-senpai, you're good at cooking."
Sakura was stunned, but she still ended up eating the food too.
I was so stressed out by everything happening, like Tohsaka's home cooking, eating together with Tohsaka, and Sakura looking downtrodden, not to mention the awkward vibe between her and Illya, that I couldn't really move much.

page6.text: As a result, I couldn't enjoy Tohsaka's excellent cooking, and spent the hour being reminded of what a flawless overachiever Rin Tohsaka is.

page7.text:
And then...
"I've got some stuff to prep in my room, so I'll turn in for the night.
We can hash out the details tomorrow morning. Get some rest, everyone."
She even washes all the dishes until they're spotless before she excuses herself.

page8.text:
"I'm going to my room, too. Everyone's tired after the forest today, so we'd better sleep early."
I don't know if that was a dig at Sakura, but Illya leaves without looking at her.

page9.text:
"...Haah. Seriously, what is going on..."
In a sense, everything's going just as Tohsaka predicted, although Illya's attitude has been weird.
The way she's treating Sakura is similar to the icy demeanor she had when we first met.

page10.text: "Why is Illya being so gruff with her when it's their first time meeting? The Einzberns and Makiris must not get along."

page11.text:
According to Kotomine, the Einzberns, Makiris, and Tohsakas were prestigious mage families that founded the Holy Grail War.
Apparently, the Einzberns had the most authority, so maybe Illya thinks of Tohsaka and Sakura as beneath her.

page12.text:
"...Haah. I hope she doesn't give you the wrong impression, Sakura. Illya can be difficult when she's in a bad mood, but I'm sure you'll get along once you talk to her.
She's just shy towards strangers—hey, Sakura?"
Sakura doesn't answer.
I watch her head waver, until she falls limply backward—

page13.text:
"Sakura...!"
I catch her by the shoulders.

page14.text:
"...Huh, Senpai? What's wrong? Why are you making such a scary face?"
...Sakura didn't even realize it.
She's asking me what's happening, as if she wasn't about to faint.

page15.text:
"...No, it's nothing."
I let go of her shoulders.
"Ah..."
Looks like that was enough to make her notice.

page16.text:
"...I'm sorry. I was a little tired, so I fell asleep."
She apologizes for something she doesn't even understand.

page17.text: "...Yeah. I bet you haven't had much rest for the last two days. You heard Tohsaka. Let's just go to sleep. You don't need to make yourself stay awake."

page18.text:
"R-right. I'll take you up on that, then. I should feel better tomorrow if I get a good night's sleep.
Since Tohsaka-senpai took care of us tonight, I'll make breakfast tomorrow morning. I'll cook the things you like for breakfast."

page19.text:
She stands up with a mischievous grin.
...Her gait is steady.
Accompanying her to her bedroom would backfire right now.
If Sakura's trying to convince me that she's okay, then I should believe her.

page20.text:
"All right. Go ahead and show her who's boss.
You're our last line of defense, Sakura. To be honest, we need to hit back at Tohsaka, or we're done for."
"You can count on me. I'll knock her out in one punch!"

page21.text:
That sounds promising... Mm, I'll do what little I can to help, too.
Let's sleep early tonight, then meet up in the kitchen at six in the morning?"
"Yes. I'll be waiting, Senpai."

page22.text:
Sakura gives me a polite bow, and then leaves for the side hallway.
Just before she's gone...
"...Um, Senpai. Please don't tell my sister what happened just earlier."
She says in a strained voice, without turning around.

page23.text:
"Yeah. You just dozed off. It isn't worth mentioning."
"...Right. Good night, Senpai."
She slides the door shut.
Sakura goes off to the guesthouse without looking back.

page24.text:
...
She must mean her fainting spell.
Sakura isn't recovering as well as she hopes.
Kotomine said that she only has days left.
Regardless of what Zouken wants to do with her, she isn't stable.

page25.text:
That's why she's been trying to put on a strong front.
She'll be fine.
That's what she insists on telling us because she doesn't want us to worry.

page26.text:
"Her sister, huh?"
Sakura never refers to Tohsaka that way except when we're alone.
And then only when something's weighing on her mind.
...When she can't stop herself from wishing for help, she calls Tohsaka her big sister.
Their complicated family background is what led to a wall being built between sisters.

page27.text:
If we can destroy that wall, then they can go back to being regular siblings.
I think that might be the best thing I can do for Sakura.
